This is a kit made by me (aadenboy), which includes 3 cloths you can use whenever!
• Lowest Quality Cloth - Lowest quality, but also the least laggy. It was the first cloth aadenboy made.
• Non-Laggy Cloth - Similar to the actual cloth, except it only spans one axis instead of two. It is less laggy, and can be used to understand these somewhat.
• Cloth - The actual cloth itself! It uses many parts (most being parts with hinges to make it swing), and the most laggiest. It works really well up until a certain extent. After some time it'll start shaking and wobbling a bunch. Use this cloth sparingly.

basically this script(when parented into backpack)
extends your hitbox so it allows raycasting to hit previous player positions

pros:
* allows clients to hit past positions of an affected player, mitigating latency issues
* easy to modify hitbox sizes, does not cost much performance(hopefully)
* can allow users to have a better experience, especially in faster paced games
   where players move fast

cons:
* hitbox size might be too big so you might actually land a shot that seems unlegit(such as hitting near the player, this could be fixed w/ tweaking hitbox sizes) 
* may not account for headshots

why?
* it mitigates latency issues w/ the server
* its a pretty cheap and easy method to make server sided hits feel nicer

note: you do not need this if you are using physics objects as they are not raycasted! (they are client authorative, not server authorative!, plus the hitboxes are cancollide false)

note that this is buggy, and is kind of a mess
but this has full on matrix interpolation and keyframe stuff, and runs on the client's renderstep so its really smooth

animating:
* you must start out with the original sample example model[you can just make your own if you want to, but thats kind of a hassle].
* there is no way to center animations yet, so you must center the model to 0,0,0[which is an issue that i will address in the future]
* use an intvalue per keyframe as that will be the way the keyframe will be looked up
* each animation must need a Config configuration and has string values indicating the part's name, and the value represents the motor affected[doesn't respect child bone stuff yet]
* every animation must be a model w/ a name that will be referred to when running an animation, default is always reserved to reset the current animation

how to run:
* on the client, set the value of the Anim stringvalue in the character
* on the server, fire all clients in character.Animation where the first argument is the animation name

how to setup: 
* AnimServer in workspace[this allows keyframes to be ran in the animation], 
* AnimHandler in Lighting[this handles all of the animations]
* Animation in StarterPack[this handles client replication of animations]
* Giver in StarterGui[this gives players an instance of animation handler]
* make a model in Lighting called Animations

When making animations keep in mind that the cframe generated from the position and orientation makes a weld that only changes C0, not C1

This also comes with a GUI for Cash & Bank Amount, and a Leaderstat script already inside.
Place everything in their corresponding services and ungroup the model.
**DO NOT ungroup the actual stuff themselves, only the models named after services once they're in the corresponding service.**

The ATM works as it should, place your card inside, the player can deposit or withdraw, and can return their card if they do not want to make a transaction.

The Money Wiring System requires you to get the player's card number (bottom left corner, its going to be a randomly generated number on the GUI under your Bank and Cash amount.) in order to make a transaction. You must have money in your bank in order to wire someone money. Enter their card number, then the amount you want to give the player, then make the transaction. There are many fail-safe systems implemented into this, you cannot enter a random number, you cannot wire money to yourself, and you cannot give someone money if you don't have the sufficient funds in your bank.

The bartender job allows any player to click on the NPC's cups, and after a random amount of time, they'll give the player money. After the player takes the money, after a randomly generated wait time, the cups will go back to normal and you can repeat the process again. **Only the player who filled the cup can take the money. **

**Better Rocket Launcher
Recently, the RetroStudio devs converted the Rocket Launcher to block coding (please please PLEASE do this for the other brickbattle tools!!!), so I decided to modify it so it had variables similarly to the Linked Sword and Paintball Gun, making it easier and more user friendly for developers. This is my first major scripting project, so please report any bugs! Included settings are: 
- ReloadTime (the time you have to wait before using it again)
- RocketSize (the size of the rocket part)
- RocketColor (the color of the rocket if team colors are disabled or you're not on a team)
- RocketSpeed (The velocity of the rocket projectile)
- FollowTeamColor (Determines whether or not the rocket is your team's color)
- ExpireTime (The time the rocket will stay loaded before automatically detonating)
- DestroyJointRadiusPercent (The radius which the blast will destroy joints)
- BlastRadius (The radius of the explosion)

The default settings are the same as the vanilla rocket launcher.

If anyone has any additional feature ideas, bug fixes, or feedback, let me know. If a RetroStudio developer is reading this, please consider converting the TimeBomb, SlingShot, and SuperBall to block coding as well! If so, I'll definitely make improved versions for all of them! I really wish we had better control over these weapons, as we can't really do much with them at the moment except use their default settings! Thank you!

Edit: No need to credit me, this model is completely free and open source. Modify and use it however you wish!

**Better SuperBall
More brickbattle tools have been converted to block coding! As with my Better Rocket Launcher, this version of the SuperBall adds a bunch of settings in order to make customizing it a lot easier. There is a strange bug where the console says that the Wait1 block in the CannonBall script isn't a number, however it is and it works as inteded otherwise. If anyone finds a way to fix this, let me know. This model is freely available and can be used or modified without any credit.

Here is a list of added settings (ReloadTime, Velocity, MaxDamage, and AllowTeamKilling were already there):

- CannonBallSize - The size of the projectile.
- CannonBallReflect - The reflection of the projectile.
- RandomColor - Determines whether the projectile is a random color. Has priority over CannonBallColor and FollowTeamColor.
- CannonBallColor - The color of the projectile. RandomColor and FollowTeamColor must be off for this to work.
- FollowTeamColor - Determines whether the projectile should be the player's team color. Has priority over CannonBallColor. RandomColor must be off for this to work.
- DespawnTime - The amount of time that will pass until a projectile despawns.
- DamageReduction (Advanced) - Every time the SuperBall bounces, the initial damage value will be divided by this number. For example, with a DamageReduction value of 2, the damage value will be halved each time it bounces off a wall or player.
- DisableThreshold (Advanced) - When the damage being done by the SuperBall is less than this number, it will become "disabled" and it will not deal damage anymore.

The default settings are the same as the vanilla SuperBall.

If anyone has any additional feature ideas, bug fixes, or feedback, let me know. Thank you to the RetroStudio developers for converting a bunch of the brickbattle tools a day after my Better Rocket Launcher was released (I guess it worked, lol), and thank you for everyone's support for my Better Rocket Launcher tool.

I have created a system which allows for creation and removal of fire using a fire setter and a fire extinguisher. The concept is an antagonistic player can set objects on fire, and other players can use fire extinguishers to put out the fires.

**Fire Stick
This tool allows the player to set parts named "BurnablePart" on fire. The fire will shrink over time, eventually despawning after 90 seconds. When a part is on fire, it will slowly damage any player which touches it. If a player is wearing a certain clothing item (http://www.roblox.com/asset/?id by default, this can be changed in KillBrickScriptFire's If3 block), they will be immune to fire. This can be used to make fireproof suits for a firefighter class. Each BurnablePart should have no more than one child in it, any more will prevent it from being set on fire. Fires created with the fire stick can be extinguished by the fire extinguisher.

This is a modified slingshot which will remove fires when its pellets make contact with a part on fire. More specifically, they will remove any object named "RemFire" or "KillBrickScriptFire". Note that I made a fire extinguisher free model a few weeks ago, however it removes all fires and objects named "KillBrickScriptFire", making it less ideal for games which have fires that shouldn't be removable.

1 - Play
2 - Pause
3 - Clear (Removes song from ActiveSong, sets TimePosition to 0 and resets to Stopped)

**Code Input Door
This is a door which only opens when you enter the correct code. The code can be changed to whatever you'd like. There is also a display which tells you what has been entered already, as well as a clear button.

Please note: There are a couple of limitations with the codes you can set. The code must be a valid positive signed integer, which basically just means your code has to be less than around 9223372036854775807. If a number larger than this is inputted into the door, it won't be handled properly. This is a limitation of Roblox's maximum integer size. Additionally, your code cannot start with 0.

The default code is 5334118 (if you get the reference, you are very cool!). You can change the code to whatever you'd like by changing the value of the CorrectCode value. You can also change the amount of time the door will stay open by changing the DoorOpenTime value. Don't mess with any other values inside the InputPanel group though, as they will break the door! You can also change the sounds the door plays by changing the sounds under the 5 key, which is located under InputPanel.

I apologize for my somewhat messy, uncommented code. It's pretty complicated, involving a lot of different scripts reading different values in order to function. I also was fighting the Roblox chat filter the whole time, so some things might be named strangely. I might try to add some documentation later on. Feel free to (attempt) to mess with the code, maybe you can make it less messy!

If you think this is cool, please consider reacting with :Retweet: to help get this on the starboard! I put a *lot* of effort into this, so I hope you enjoy using it! Let me know if you need any help or if I messed something up.

The Admin Gui has 23 default command but you can easily add more commands for you games like Ban.

**How To Add Your Own Command**

https://discord.com/channels/645632117455323136/1081243511858397264/1081243634684399656

1. Go to "Lighting" and copy the "Test" StringValue. Now put it in "Commands" in Lighting. After that change the name to what ever your command is called (ex. Ban) and change the value to the description of your command (ex. Bans the given player from the game)

2. Now add values in your command that we just added "Inputs" folder (We support all values). If you want people to be able to choose players add a "StringValue" then add a "BooleanValue" and name it "PlayerValue" and then add another "BooleanValue" and name it "All" and set it to true if you want it to be able to choose "All"

3. Go edit "AdminScript" in Workspace and add "Do Not Run" block and name it to your command name. Why? Because when executing the command it will execute the Do Not Run block with the same name.

4. Now its time to script. Sent input from the gui will be a table so to get an input from the sent inputs you must use "Get Table Value" the key as the Input name (ex. Key: Player | Value: target). If you are using a PlayerValue Then create another Do Not 
Run block that will do the actual command (ex. BanPlrFromGame). For the first Do Not Run block get the player from the inputs and add a new "Set Variable" block below that and set the "VariableName" to "func" and set the value to the name of the second block. Confused? just copy one.

- Constantly sends information when input is changed which may cause lag so don't spam please
- Sending information and loading the values are all server sided so if the server is slow then its gonna lag
- Aspect ratio is poopy on other devices other than desktop
- No "Others" option for PlayerValue

```basic quest system
create quests that will reward leaderstats on completion. could be modified to reward items and the likes but i didn't do that so go die.

quests will be structured as so: (several example quests given in free model)

----
QuestName [folder]
  Rewards [folder]
    Leaderstats [folder]
      LeaderStatName [NumberValue] [Value = reward given]
  RequiredFlags [folder]
     FirstFlag [BoolValue] [= false] [name = name of flag required to complete quest]
     SecondFlag [BoolValue] [= false] [same deal^]
     ...
  FlagToActivate [StringValue] [= name of flag fired to assign quest to player]
  Repeatable [BoolValue]
  Description [folder]
    FlavorText [StringValue] [value displays as quest body in gui]
    ObjectiveText [StringValue] [same deal ^]
    Sender [StringValue] [doubly same deal ^]
----

quests are basically trackers for flag strings sent to the Quests.fireFlag(player :Player, flagString :string) event. when a string is sent to the event, it'll check for quests where FlagToActivate.Value = flagString, and then assign them to the player.

  it'll then check the RequiredFlags of any quest assigned to the player, and if requiredFlag.Name = flagString, it'll set its value to true.
 
  if all requiredFlag.Value 's = true then quest is completable, firing remoteEvent questCompleted(player, quest), requiring the player's client to fire Quests.completeQuest (player :Player, currentQuest :Quest Folder) to fully complete it

  when the quest is completed, it will fire Quest.fireFlag() with the player who completed it and the name of the quest, so a quest can be required to be completed for another quest or a quest can assign another quest as well.

  calling Quests.savePlayerQuests(player) will save all of the player's quests to a data store so progress isn't lost
etc etc.
```

Mig's Program Maker

**Mig's program maker, which is a text-based coding app, can be used to make programs such as importing objects, do repeating actions (it works slightly good), print, send messages and other functions!**
--
**Can the project/app be modified?**
*It is open-source, since it's aimed to players interested into how retrostudio coding works/how to create something like this will be able to learn :)*
--
**How does this work?**
The program maker uses a script to read the lines inserted, run functions (it is also VERY case-sensitive) and finally, print an output.
--
**How good is it?**
To be fair, in my persepective, I think it is great as it is an advancement from the kind of models you will find in here, there was a lot of effort put into this project.
Performance-wise, I think it's low, due to Retrostudio's restrictions and just how Roblox handles client stuff bla bla bla. It's just a fun project so create your small programs, show it to the world and have fun! 
--
**Note from the Creator:** 
If you ever import this app/plugin or whatever you'd like to name this, I would be really happy! As my goal for this is to prove text-based coding can be possible (this idea stemmed from an argument i saw on #retro-chat hehe)

I'd also like to add that this program maker isn't the best but you can create functions in the main script and save programs which is already good :)

Regarding add-ons, as I said earlier, you can add your own functions and have fun tweaking it! You can also republish this project of mine with your own edited version (you must credit me though :TrollSad: and I would allow a tweaked version if the changes made on the program maker are significant enough to be considered add-ons!)

Thank you and I hope you enjoy using the first ever public model of text-based coding :) :Retweet:
